candidates.tagline: $499 toothbrush with a camera watches you brush at 28fps — floss was too simple
candidates.story: Dyson launched the CameraJet on September 1, 2026 — a $499 electric toothbrush with a 100,000-pixel AI camera that fires precision mouthrinse jets at detected plaque gaps, backed by 16 million lines of code, 470,000 dental training images, and a team of fluid dynamicists — to automate what dental floss does for about $3.
candidates.why_funny: Dyson recruited ML engineers, fluid dynamicists, and Singapore's National University to build a product whose core value proposition is 'we noticed you weren't flossing and decided the answer was a camera in your mouth.'
candidates.alt: Two Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrushes in Ceramic Ultra Blue standing next to a bathroom sink, showing the compact design with an AI camera module mounted beneath the brush head

candidates.tagline: Google said '3× stronger'. It cracked in the same spot. For the fourth year.
candidates.story: Google's Pixel 11 Pro Fold launched August 12, 2026 at $1,799 with marketing claiming it was '3× stronger' than its predecessor; on August 21, durability tester JerryRigEverything bent it and it cracked along the exact same antenna line near the hinge as the Pixel Fold, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, and Pixel 10 Pro Fold — with the outer display popping off completely for good measure.
candidates.why_funny: For four consecutive generations Google has launched a foldable phone, promised meaningful structural improvements, and then watched it crack in precisely the same spot when someone pushes on it — which is a remarkably consistent way to be wrong.
candidates.alt: Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold under lateral stress during a bend test, showing visible deformation at the antenna line next to the hinge where the device cracked, with the outer display partially separating
